name: The Wardenswatch
description: Extramural, and unlawful. Six years ago there was nothing outside the Hallowgate but the lazar house and a cart track. There are perhaps nineteen hundred people from Drennmark living here now, in a suburb the League's charter says does not exist, and Waerhaven feeds it because Waerhaven needs the hands. Everyone here left somewhere, and everyone here is facing north.

wardens_road.name: Wardens' Road
wardens_road.description: The cart track that was here before the people were, running south from the gate between two rows of what began as lean-tos against the city wall and have become, without anybody deciding it, a street. Turf roofs, stove pipes through them, and a drainage ditch dug by somebody who knew how, straight and graded and better made than anything the city has done out here.
wardens_road.first_visit: You come out of the gate arch expecting country and get a street: smoke, children, a woman splitting kindling, and nineteen hundred people that Waerhaven's own charter says are not standing here.
ambience: Everyone in sight is doing something with their hands and nobody is doing it for wages.
Somebody is teaching a child a Drennmark counting rhyme and correcting the numbers.
A face at a doorway checks the gate arch behind you to see whether you came alone.
The ditch has been re-dug since the last rain, further out, by somebody who expects a worse one.

exits.label: South, out to the lazar house

the_grey_hall.name: The Grey Hall
the_grey_hall.description: A converted timber barn that is, in every practical sense, Drennmark's embassy to a city that has never agreed to receive one. The Grey Wardens keep a table at the north end, a map on the wall with the Wyrdpines drawn on it in more detail than the Charthouse has ever managed, and a written record of every person who has come south, where from, and on what day. Warden Aske Vorn keeps that record. She will not show it.
ambience: The map on the wall has pins in it, and a line of pins that stops, and nothing beyond the line.
A Warden comes in off the road, is given food before being asked anything, and eats it before saying anything.
Somebody reads a list aloud, quietly, at the end of the room, and is not interrupted.

exits.label: Round the back, to the chapel

chapel_of_the_grey_road.name: Chapel of the Grey Road
chapel_of_the_grey_road.description: A shed with a painted door, where Drennmark's road-god is asked for a way back. The god is not asked for protection and is not asked for plenty. He is asked, specifically and only, for a road home, and the asking is done aloud, in turn, by name of the place. The Wardens meet here when they do not want to meet at the Grey Hall, which is a thing the Watch has not worked out and Aske Vorn has never bothered to hide.
ambience: Somebody names a village aloud and the room repeats it back and that is the whole of the service.
The painted door has been repainted this year. The paint is Waerhaven paint and the pattern is not.
There is no offering box. There is a shelf of things people have left anyway.

exits.label: Back round to the Grey Hall

the_green_bough.name: The Green Bough
the_green_bough.description: A Drennmark house, in a Drennmark suburb, serving Drennmark beer badly, out of a building that was three lean-tos last winter. Everyone in it left somewhere. Ask why and the room does not go hostile — it goes quiet, and stays quiet, and then somebody changes the subject kindly, and you understand that you have been answered.
ambience: The beer is genuinely bad and served with the pride of a thing done properly a long way from home.
Somebody asks after a village by name and is told a number instead of an answer.
A man sits with his back to the wall and his face to the door and is not the only one.

the_lazar_house.name: The Lazar House
the_lazar_house.description: Built well outside the wall in a kinder century, for the sick nobody wanted inside it, and empty for sixty years until six years ago. It is full now, and not with lepers, and the almoners who keep it will tell you that they are not sure what with. The people in the long room came south later than the rest and further, and most of them do not talk, and the ones who do all describe the same weather.
ambience: The long room is warm, and quiet, and full, and nobody in it is dying of anything anyone can name.
An almoner counts blankets, comes up short, and counts again rather than say the number.
Somebody in the far bed describes snow, in a warm month, in detail, to nobody.
